scope: Reviewed named variants and interactions, target Bedrock 1.26.52; no future Frostbite/Freezing-effect rules.

variants.answer: Frogs have temperate (orange), warm (white) and cold (green) forms. A tadpole’s growth biome determines its frog form; the parents’ colors do not determine it.

froglights.answer: A temperate orange frog makes ochre froglights, a warm white frog makes pearlescent froglights, and a cold green frog makes verdant froglights. The frog must eat a small magma cube.

identity.answer: A temperate frog is the orange frog variant.

spawning.answer: Find temperate frogs in ordinary swamps, or raise a tadpole in a temperate biome such as plains or forest.

variants.answer: This is the temperate, orange frog. Its growth biome sets its form.

froglights.answer: A temperate frog produces a ochre froglight when it eats a small magma cube. Froglights are produced by that interaction, not ordinary frog death loot.

identity.answer: A warm frog is the white frog variant.

spawning.answer: Find warm frogs in mangrove swamps, or raise a tadpole in a warm biome such as a desert or jungle.

variants.answer: This is the warm, white frog. Its growth biome sets its form.

froglights.answer: A warm frog produces a pearlescent froglight when it eats a small magma cube. Froglights are produced by that interaction, not ordinary frog death loot.

identity.answer: A cold frog is the green frog variant.

spawning.answer: Raise a tadpole in a cold biome such as snowy plains or a grove. Ordinary natural frog spawning is in swamps and mangrove swamps; boundary conditions can affect the resulting form.

variants.answer: This is the cold, green frog. Its growth biome sets its form.

froglights.answer: A cold frog produces a verdant froglight when it eats a small magma cube. Froglights are produced by that interaction, not ordinary frog death loot.

hatching.answer: Frogspawn hatches into tadpoles in water. Carry a tadpole in a water bucket; the biome where it grows up determines whether its frog form is temperate, warm or cold.

variants.answer: Axolotls come in pink/leucistic, brown, gold, cyan and blue. The first four occur naturally; blue is obtained through breeding rather than natural spawning.

identity.answer: This is the pink axolotl color variant.

spawning.answer: Look for pink axolotls in suitable lush-cave water with clay nearby underneath. This is a naturally spawning color, not a separate biome-exclusive species.

variants.answer: Its color does not give it different ordinary health or attack abilities.

identity.answer: This is the brown axolotl color variant.

variants.answer: Its color does not give it different ordinary health or attack abilities.

variants.answer: Its color does not give it different ordinary health or attack abilities.

spawning.answer: Look for cyan axolotls in suitable lush-cave water with clay nearby underneath. This is a naturally spawning color, not a separate biome-exclusive species.

variants.answer: Its color does not give it different ordinary health or attack abilities.

identity.answer: This is the blue axolotl color variant.

spawning.answer: Blue axolotls do not spawn naturally. Breed adult axolotls using buckets of tropical fish. A baby has a 1-in-1,200 blue-mutation chance; blue parents can also pass their color to offspring.

Foxes have red and snow (white) forms. Red foxes occur in taigas, old growth pine/spruce taigas and dappled forests; snow foxes occur in snowy taigas and groves. Breeding inherits a parent’s form.

identity.answer: A red fox is the ordinary orange-red fox variant.

spawning.answer: Find red foxes in taigas, old growth pine taigas, old growth spruce taigas and dappled forests.

identity.answer: A snow fox is the white fox variant.

spawning.answer: Find snow foxes in snowy taigas and groves. Breeding foxes can inherit a parent’s form; moving an adult to snow does not recolor it.

variants.answer: Chickens have temperate, warm and cold forms. Natural spawning chooses the form from the biome; breeding inherits a parent’s form, and moving an adult does not recolor it.

identity.answer: This is the temperate chicken variant.

spawning.answer: Look for temperate chickens in plains, sunflower plains, forest, flower forest, birch forest, old growth birch forest, dark forest, swamp. Those are natural-spawning habitats; a spawn egg can choose this form in additional biomes without making those natural spawning sites.

variants.answer: Breeding inherits a parent’s variant; transporting an adult to another climate does not change its form.

identity.answer: This is the warm chicken variant.

spawning.answer: Look for warm chickens in savanna, savanna plateau, windswept savanna, jungle, sparse jungle, bamboo jungle, badlands, eroded badlands, wooded badlands. Natural rabbit coats are brown, black, salt, white, white splotched and gold. Gold is the desert form; white forms occur in snowy biomes. Toast is a name-tag appearance. A hostile killer bunny is not available in ordinary Bedrock gameplay.

identity.answer: This is the brown rabbit coat.

spawning.answer: Look in flower forests, taigas, meadows, cherry groves and dappled forests.

identity.answer: This is the black rabbit coat.

spawning.answer: Look in flower forests, taigas, meadows, cherry groves and dappled forests.

identity.answer: This is the salt rabbit coat.

spawning.answer: Look in flower forests, taigas, meadows, cherry groves and dappled forests.

identity.answer: This is the white rabbit coat.

spawning.answer: Look in snowy plains, ice spikes, snowy taigas, groves or snowy slopes. Bedrock also allows rabbits in snowy beaches, frozen oceans and frozen rivers.

identity.answer: Toast is a named rabbit appearance.

naming.answer: Use the exact name Toast to get the special appearance. The name does not change its ordinary behavior.

identity.answer: A hostile killer bunny is not available in ordinary Bedrock gameplay.

spawning.answer: The killer bunny is not an ordinary Bedrock rabbit variant and does not naturally spawn in Bedrock.

combat.answer: Normal Bedrock rabbits are passive. There is no ordinary hostile killer-bunny variant available here.

variants.answer: Villagers have seven biome appearances, thirteen professions, and unemployed/nitwit states. Biome clothing and profession are separate. A swamp-looking villager is not a separate swamp-exclusive profession.

spawning.answer: Find a armorer in villages, or let an eligible unemployed adult claim an available blast furnace. The profession is not confined to a single biome.

construction.answer: Provide an available blast furnace to an eligible unemployed adult villager. Babies and nitwits cannot take that job; prior trading can lock an existing profession.

trading.answer: A armorer trades armor, depending on its level and selected offers. It needs its claimed blast furnace to work and restock; every armorer does not have identical offers.
